Third Quarter 2026 Results
Press Release
             
Banc of California, Inc. Reports Third Quarter Diluted Earnings per Share of $0.46, Up 21% Year Over Year
Strategic Repositioning and Core Business Performance Drive Higher Earnings and Positive Operating Leverage
Company Release – 10/27/2026
Quarter Results

LOS ANGELES, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Banc of California, Inc. (NYSE: BANC) (“Banc of California” or the “Company”), the
parent company of wholly-owned subsidiary Banc of California (the “Bank”), today reported financial results for the third quarter ended
September 30, 2026. The Company reported net earnings available to common and equivalent stockholders of $73.1 million, or $0.46 per
diluted common share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $59.7 million, or $0.38 per diluted common share for the third quarter of
2025. For the second quarter of 2026, the Company reported a net loss available to common and equivalent stockholders of $251.3 million,
or $(1.61) per diluted common share, reflecting the previously announced strategic balance sheet repositioning.
Jared Wolff, Chairman & CEO of Banc of California, commented, “Our third quarter results demonstrate the stronger earnings foundation
we have created through our second quarter strategic balance sheet repositioning and continued execution across our business. Compared
to the first quarter, before the repositioning, diluted earnings per share increased 18%, total revenue increased 6% and pre-tax pre-
provision income increased 12%. We also grew deposits, reduced our reliance on brokered funding and increased our CET1 ratio by 45
basis points from the second quarter.”
Mr. Wolff added, “We expect further improvement in profitability in the fourth quarter as we realize a full quarter of earnings from our
securities reinvestment and additional benefits from the completed loan sales. We are focused on building on this progress through deeper
client relationships, disciplined loan growth, growth in relationship deposits and continued capital generation to deliver sustainable
earnings growth and long-term shareholder value.”
Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights:
•The second quarter strategic balance sheet repositioning contributed to increased third quarter earnings, with diluted earnings
per share of $0.46, up 21% from $0.38 year-over-year.
•Total revenue of $303.8 million, up 6% year-over-year, and pre-tax pre-provision income(1) of $118.4 million, up 16% year-
over-year, while noninterest expense of $185.4 million remained flat year-over-year.
•Net interest income increased $21.9 million, or 9%, from prior quarter to $272.4 million, and net interest margin expanded 21
basis points to 3.34%, reflecting higher yields on investment securities following the Company's second quarter strategic balance
sheet repositioning activities and continued execution across the business.
•Loans and leases held for investment increased $379.7 million, or 6% on an annualized basis, driven by $2.6 billion of loan
production and disbursements with a weighted average interest rate on production of 6.58%.
•Average deposits increased $565.3 million, or 8% on an annualized basis, supporting reduced wholesale funding.
•Credit quality trends were favorable, as nonperforming and classified loans and leases as a percentage of total loans and leases held
for investment declined by 12 basis points and 35 basis points, respectively.
•Capital ratios(2) increased from prior quarter and exceeded the regulatory thresholds for "well capitalized" banks, including an
estimated 12.10% Tier 1 capital ratio, up 43 basis points from prior quarter, and 9.70% common equity tier 1 ("CET1") capital ratio, up
45 basis points from the prior quarter, reflecting capital generation following the balance sheet repositioning.
(1) Non-GAAP measure; refer to section 'Non-GAAP Measures'
(2) Capital ratios for September 30, 2026 are preliminary
                                              2
During the second quarter of 2026, the Company entered into targeted loan sales relating to $827 million of commercial real estate and
construction loans. Of these loans, approximately $525 million were sold during the third quarter. Of the remaining approximately $300
million of construction loans, $235 million were sold on October 21, 2026, and $65 million were removed prior to sale as construction on
the project was completed and the loan converted into permanent financing. We anticipate selling our remaining held for sale loan portfolio
over the next several quarters.

Net Interest Income and Margin
Third Quarter of 2026 Compared to Second Quarter of 2026
Net interest income increased by $21.9 million to $272.4 million for the third quarter, from $250.5 million in the second quarter. This
increase was primarily driven by the $17.7 million increase in interest income on investment securities resulting from the strategic balance
sheet repositioning during the second quarter and reinvestment into higher-yielding assets, including a $2.8 million special dividend
received on FHLB stock. In addition, interest income on loans increased by $7.7 million primarily driven by lower interest reversals
associated with nonaccrual loans compared to the prior quarter and one additional day in the quarter. These increases were offset partially
by a $6.0 million increase in interest expense on deposits primarily due to increased market interest rates, one additional day in the quarter,
as well as higher average balances.
Net interest margin was 3.34% for the third quarter, up 21 basis points from 3.13% for the second quarter. The increase was primarily
driven by the higher yield on average interest earning assets, which increased to 5.43% from 5.18%, reflecting a 142 basis point increase in
the average yield on investment securities to 4.86%. The increase in investment securities yield reflects earnings from the strategic balance
sheet repositioning and reinvestment activities.
The average total cost of funds increased to 2.16% from 2.14%, primarily due to a 3 basis point increase in the average total cost of
deposits to 1.83%. Average total deposits increased by $565.3 million, with a $546.3 million increase in average interest-bearing deposits.
The increase in average yield on total interest-bearing deposits reflects the impact of the federal funds rate increases during the quarter.
Average noninterest-bearing deposits represented 28.0% of average total deposits in the third quarter, down from 28.5% in the second
quarter.

YTD September 30, 2026 vs YTD September 30, 2025
Net interest income increased $48.5 million to $774.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $726.0 million for the
nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by a $53.8 million decrease in interest expense on deposits due
to lower interest rates following federal funds rate cuts in the second half of 2025, and a $30.6 million increase in interest income from
investment securities reflecting the benefits of prior balance sheet repositioning and reinvestment activities, including $4.1 million of
special dividends received on FHLB stock. These benefits were offset partially by a $15.5 million increase in borrowing costs associated
with funding loan growth and the subordinated debt redemption prior to higher repricing in the second quarter of 2026, a $13.8 million
decrease in loan interest income primarily attributable to a reversal of previously accrued interest on loans placed on nonaccrual status
offset partially by the benefit of higher average loan balances, and an $11.8 million decrease in interest income from deposits in financial
institutions due to lower balances and lower market interest rates.
The net interest margin was 3.24% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up 11 basis points from 3.13% for the nine months
ended September 30, 2025. The year-over-year improvement was primarily driven by a 26 basis point decrease in the average total cost of
funds due mainly to lower market interest rates and a 69 basis point increase in the average yield on investment securities.
The average total cost of funds decreased by 26 basis points to 2.14%, driven primarily by the decline in average cost of deposits of 30
basis points to 1.81%, reflecting the impact of lower market interest rates. Average total deposits increased by $536.6 million year-over-
year, as a result of a $316.6 million increase in average interest-bearing deposits and a $220.1 million increase in average noninterest-
bearing deposits. Average noninterest-bearing deposits represented 28.4% of average total deposits for the nine months ended September
30, 2026, up from 28.2% for the comparable period in 2025. The average cost of borrowings also decreased by 49 basis points to 4.50%,
reflecting the paydown of higher-cost borrowings in the prior year and their replacement with lower-cost short-term Federal Home Loan
Bank ("FHLB") advances.
The average yield on interest-earning assets declined by 15 basis points to 5.29%. The decrease was primarily driven by a 27 basis point
decline in average yield on loans and leases to 5.69% and a 74 basis point decline in average yield on deposits in financial institutions,
primarily consisting of reserves held at the Federal Reserve Bank, to 3.65%, reflecting lower market rates. These decreases were offset
partially by a 69 basis point increase in the average yield on investment securities to 3.90%, reflecting a benefit from the strategic balance
sheet repositioning and reinvestment activities.

Provision For Credit Losses
Third Quarter of 2026 Compared to Second Quarter of 2026
The provision for credit losses was $10.4 million for the third quarter compared to $161.8 million for the second quarter.
The third quarter provision included an $8.4 million provision for loan losses and a $2.0 million provision for unfunded commitments. The
provision was primarily driven by net charge-off activity experienced in the quarter and growth in the held for investment ("HFI") loan
portfolio, offset partially by lower specific reserves and changes in the economic factors used in the provision estimate.
The second quarter provision was elevated by the strategic balance sheet repositioning activities related to the targeted loan sale process,
the impact of loan growth and higher loss given default rates on commercial real estate and multi-family construction loans, offset partially
by improved risk ratings in our HFI portfolio.
YTD September 30, 2026 vs YTD September 30, 2025
The provision for credit losses was $182.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $58.1 million for the nine
months ended September 30, 2025. The provision for the 2026 period included a provision for loan losses of $180.2 million, reflecting the
impact of the targeted loan sale process and the impact of loan growth, offset partially by improved risk ratings for our HFI portfolio.
The provision for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 included the impact of $506.7 million of loans transferred to held for sale
("HFS") and recorded at the lower of cost or market value. The remaining increase in the provision for credit losses was primarily driven
by net charge-off activity experienced in the first half of the year, with additional impacts from changes in loan risk ratings. These were
offset partially by lower specific reserves and a favorable shift in the portfolio mix due to growth in loan segments with lower expected
credit losses.
                                              6
Noninterest Income
Third Quarter of 2026 Compared to Second Quarter of 2026
Noninterest income increased by $265.5 million to $31.4 million for the third quarter, compared to a loss of $234.1 million for the second
quarter. The increase was primarily driven by a $257.5 million decrease in loss on securities and an $8.3 million decrease in loss on loans
and leases HFS, both of which were a result of the strategic balance sheet repositioning actions taken in the second quarter. Also included
in noninterest income was a $2.0 million increase in operating lease income, primarily due to new lease fundings and higher lease renewal
income, offset partially by a $1.4 million decrease in other income. The decrease in other income was primarily due to the second quarter
gain recognized on the sale of the Company's single-family mortgage servicing rights portfolio, offset partially by the second quarter loss
on the redemption of the $385 million subordinated note.
YTD September 30, 2026 vs YTD September 30, 2025
Noninterest income decreased by $268.0 million to a loss of $167.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to
income of $100.6 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to the $256.0 million pre-tax loss
recognized as part of the securities repositioning and a $16.6 million increase in the loss on loans and leases HFS resulting primarily from
lower of cost or market adjustments recorded during the second quarter in connection with the strategic balance sheet repositioning actions.
Noninterest Expense
Third Quarter of 2026 Compared to Second Quarter of 2026
Noninterest expense decreased by $4.5 million to $185.4 million for the third quarter from $189.9 million for the second quarter. The
decrease was primarily due to a $5.1 million decrease in other expense due to a non-recurring software obsolescence charge taken during
the second quarter and a $2.3 million decrease in insurance and assessments due to a lower FDIC assessment rate resulting from favorable
mix. These decreases were offset partially by a $2.2 million increase in compensation expense primarily driven by one-time incentive plan
adjustments in the second quarter and a $1.6 million increase in operating lease and customer related expenses.
YTD September 30, 2026 vs YTD September 30, 2025
Noninterest expense increased by $1.4 million to $556.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $555.2 million for
the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to an $8.2 million increase in other expense related mainly to
software obsolescence charges, a $7.8 million increase in insurance and assessments due to the higher assessment rate resulting from the
balance sheet repositioning and its effect on assessment related metrics, and a $2.2 million increase in loan expense related to legal fees.
These increases were offset partially by a $7.9 million decrease in customer related expenses primarily due to federal funds rate cuts in the
fourth quarter of 2025 and a $3.6 million decrease in leased equipment depreciation.
Income Taxes
Third Quarter of 2026 Compared to Second Quarter of 2026
Income tax expense of $25.0 million was recorded for the third quarter, resulting in an effective tax rate of 23.1%, compared to an income
tax benefit of $93.9 million and an effective tax rate of 28.0% for the second quarter. The second quarter tax rate reflects the effects of the
Company's balance sheet repositioning actions. Due to the significant impact of these actions on projected annual earnings, in the second
quarter, the Company began calculating its income tax provision using the year-to-date effective tax rate approach rather than the estimated
annual effective tax rate method. The decrease in the effective tax rate from the second quarter is due primarily to the recognition of
increased income tax benefits in the third quarter.
YTD September 30, 2026 vs YTD September 30, 2025
Income tax benefit of $45.1 million was recorded for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, resulting in an effective tax rate of
34.3%, compared to income tax expense of $61.7 million and an effective tax rate of 28.9% for the same period in 2025. The increase in
the effective tax rate from 2025 to 2026 is due primarily to the effects of the Company’s balance sheet repositioning actions taken in the
second quarter of 2026.

Securities
Available-for-sale ("AFS") securities increased by $0.6 billion during the third quarter to $5.1 billion at September 30, 2026 compared to
$4.5 billion at June 30, 2026, due primarily to the remaining reinvestment activities following the securities repositioning in the second
quarter. During the third quarter AFS securities were impacted by $997.2 million of purchases offset partially by $209.9 million of
principal paydowns, $160.2 million decrease in the fair value of AFS securities, $26.8 million of maturities, and $18.3 million of sales. As
of September 30, 2026, AFS securities had aggregate unrealized net after-tax losses in AOCI of $261.4 million, up from $145.3 million at
June 30, 2026, driven by higher interest rates.

Total loans and leases HFI increased by $379.7 million in the third quarter to $24.6 billion at September 30, 2026. The increase reflected
continued growth in the Company's other residential real estate mortgage loans and asset-based lending portfolios, as well as growth in the
other commercial portfolio during the quarter. Loan production and disbursements totaled $2.6 billion in the third quarter and were broad-
based, with a weighted average interest rate on production of 6.58%.
                                              9
Total loans and leases HFS decreased by $416.4 million in the third quarter and totaled $498.8 million at September 30, 2026. The
decrease was primarily driven by the sale of loans associated with the Company's previously announced $827 million targeted loan sale.
Approximately $525 million were sold during the third quarter. Of the remaining approximately $300 million of construction loans, $235
million were sold on October 21, 2026, and $65 million were removed prior to sale as construction on the project was completed and the
loan converted into permanent financing. We anticipate selling our remaining held for sale loan portfolio over the next several quarters.

Credit quality trends were favorable in the third quarter reflecting both portfolio actions and underlying migration in the third quarter.
Nonperforming and classified loans and leases as a percentage of total loans and leases HFI decreased 12 basis points and 35 basis points,
respectively, while special mention loans increased 19 basis points.
At September 30, 2026, total delinquent loans and leases were $114.8 million, compared to $173.7 million at June 30, 2026. The 30 to 89
days delinquent category decreased by $35.4 million in other residential real estate mortgage loans, $5.8 million in asset-based loans, $3.1
million in commercial real estate mortgage loans, and $2.5 million in other commercial loans. In the 90 or more days delinquent category,
there were decreases of $11.5 million in other commercial loans, $4.9 million in multi-family real estate mortgage loans, and $1.3 million
in commercial real estate mortgage loans, offset partially by an increase of $5.2 million in other residential real estate mortgage loans.
At September 30, 2026, nonperforming loans and leases were $177.2 million, compared to $203.7 million at June 30, 2026. During the
third quarter, nonperforming loans and leases decreased by $26.5 million due to transfers to loans HFS of $55.0 million, charge-offs of
$17.8 million, paydowns of $11.9 million, and transfers to accrual status of $11.0 million, offset partially by additions of $69.3 million.
At September 30, 2026, nonperforming assets were $198.7 million, or 0.57% of total assets, compared to $220.0 million, or 0.63% of total
assets, as of June 30, 2026. At September 30, 2026, nonperforming assets included $21.5 million of foreclosed assets, consisting primarily
of single-family residences.

The allowance for credit losses - loans, which includes the reserve for unfunded loan commitments, totaled $269.3 million, or 1.10% of
total loans and leases HFI at September 30, 2026, compared to $276.2 million, or 1.14% of total loans and leases HFI at June 30, 2026.
The $6.9 million decrease in the allowance was driven by net charge-offs of $17.3 million, of which $10.0 million had been specifically
reserved as of June 30, 2026, offset partially by the provision of $10.4 million.
In addition to the associated provisions in our ACL, our ability to absorb certain credit losses is also bolstered by (i) $109.9 million of loss
coverage from the credit-linked notes associated with the $2.1 billion of single-family residential mortgage loans in our portfolio; and (ii)
unearned credit marks of $11.7 million on $1.2 billion of purchased loans without credit deterioration.
The ACL coverage of nonperforming loans and leases was 152% at September 30, 2026 compared to 136% at June 30, 2026. Net charge-
offs were 0.27% of average loans and leases (annualized) for the third quarter, compared to net charge-offs of 2.54% for the second
quarter. The quarter-over-quarter improvement was primarily attributable to the impact of the targeted loan sale process in the second
quarter.

Total deposits increased by $139.1 million to $28.3 billion at September 30, 2026 from $28.1 billion at June 30, 2026, driven primarily by
an increase in interest-bearing deposits of $206.5 million and a decrease in noninterest-bearing deposits of $67.4 million. Interest-bearing
deposits increased due mainly to higher balances in money market accounts of $582.2 million, checking accounts of $284.7 million, and
savings accounts of $28.0 million, offset partially by lower brokered and non-brokered time deposits of $688.4 million.
At September 30, 2026, noninterest-bearing checking deposits totaled $7.7 billion, or 27% of total deposits, compared to $7.8 billion, or
28% of total deposits, at June 30, 2026.
At September 30, 2026, uninsured and uncollateralized deposits totaled $7.3 billion, or 26% of total deposits, compared to $7.6 billion, or
27% of total deposits, at June 30, 2026.
In addition to deposit products, we also offer alternative, non-depository corporate treasury solutions for select clients to invest excess
liquidity. These off-balance sheet client funds totaled $1.0 billion at September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2026, respectively.
Borrowings
Borrowings decreased by $51.7 million to $2.4 billion at September 30, 2026 from $2.5 billion at June 30, 2026, driven primarily by the
repayment of a maturing long-term FHLB advance.
                                              12
Equity
During the third quarter, total stockholders’ equity decreased by $61.3 million to $3.3 billion and tangible common equity(1) decreased by
$55.1 million to $2.5 billion at September 30, 2026. The decrease in total stockholders’ equity for the third quarter resulted primarily from
an increase in the aggregate unrealized net after-tax loss in AOCI for AFS securities of $116.1 million and common and preferred stock
dividends of $29.3 million, offset partially by net earnings of $83.1 million.
At September 30, 2026, book value per common share decreased to $17.99 compared to $18.38 at June 30, 2026, and tangible book value
per common share(1) decreased to $16.09 compared to $16.44 at June 30, 2026. The decrease was primarily driven by the increased
aggregate unrealized net after-tax loss in AOCI on our portfolio of AFS securities.
For the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, the Company repurchased 1,709,935 shares of common and common equivalent
stock at a weighted average price per share of $18.68, or $31.9 million in the aggregate. As of September 30, 2026, $82.6 million remained
available under the current stock repurchase authorization, which expires in March 2027.

About Banc of California, Inc.
Banc of California, Inc. (NYSE: BANC) is a bank holding company with over $34 billion in assets and the parent company of Banc of
California. Banc of California is one of the nation’s premier relationship-based business banks, providing banking and treasury
management services to small, middle-market, and venture-backed businesses. Through its Private Banking division, the bank also serves
individuals and families with personalized banking solutions, dedicated relationship management, and exceptional service. Banc of
California is the largest publicly-traded bank headquartered in Los Angeles and the third largest bank headquartered in California and
offers a broad range of loan and deposit products and services through 76 full-service branches located throughout California and in
Denver, Colorado, and Durham, North Carolina, as well as through regional offices nationwide. The bank also provides full-service
payment processing solutions to its clients and serves the Community Association Management industry nationwide with its technology-
forward platform, SmartStreet™. The bank is committed to its local communities through the Banc of California Charitable Foundation,
and by supporting organizations that provide financial literacy and job training, small business support, affordable housing, and more.
Member FDIC. For more information, please visit us at www.bancofcal.com.

base, including among our venture banking and private banking clients, or other low cost funding sources necessary to fund our activities
particularly in a rising or high interest rate environment; (vii) the rapid withdrawal of a significant amount of demand deposits over a short
period of time; (viii) our ability to achieve or maintain the anticipated benefits of our strategic repositioning due to one or more of the other

BANC OF CALIFORNIA, INC.
NON-GAAP MEASURES
We refer to certain financial measures that are not recognized under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) in this press
release, including: tangible common equity, tangible book value per common share, return on average tangible common equity, pre-tax
pre-provision income, and efficiency ratio. These non-GAAP measures are used by management in its analysis of the Company's
performance.
Tangible common equity is total stockholders' equity less preferred stock, goodwill and intangible assets. Tangible book value per common
share is calculated by dividing tangible common equity by common shares outstanding. Return on average tangible common equity is
calculated by dividing net earnings available to common stockholders, after adjustment for amortization of intangible assets and any
goodwill impairment, by average tangible common equity. Banking regulators also exclude goodwill and other intangible assets from
stockholders' equity when assessing the capital adequacy of a financial institution.
Pre-tax pre-provision income is calculated by subtracting noninterest expense from total revenue, which is the sum of net interest income
and noninterest income.
Efficiency ratio is calculated by dividing noninterest expense (less intangible asset amortization and acquisition, integration and
reorganization costs) by total revenue (the sum of net interest income and noninterest income, less gain (loss) on securities AFS).
Management believes the presentation of these financial measures provides useful supplemental information that is helpful to an
understanding of the financial results and operating performance of the Company. This disclosure should not be viewed as a substitute for
results determined in accordance with GAAP, nor is it necessarily comparable to non-GAAP performance measures that may be presented
by other companies.
The following tables provide reconciliations of the non-GAAP measures to financial measures defined by GAAP.
